question: Under what condition does determinate cognition of the form 'I know this thus' arise?
premises: Determinate cognition takes the form 'I know this thus.'
Such cognition depends on reflection arising through the six sheaths.
The six sheaths condition the limited atom.
inference: Therefore determinate cognition arises when reflection occurs through the limiting structure of the six sheaths.
uncertainties: The compound ṣaṭkañcukābilāṇūtthapratibimbanato is compressed; the causal chain is interpreted in line with standard Trika doctrine.
plain_english: When a determinate cognition arises in the form 'I know this in this way,' it does so through a reflection that comes up from the limited self under the conditioning of the six sheaths.
